gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Asustor's USB4 ports on the Flashstor Gen2 and Lockerstor Gen3 cannot link a PC or Mac at all (AMD's USB4 driver allows only external drives and NAS-to-NAS), nor that QNAP's Thunderbolt NAS line needs macOS 13.5 or later and tops out at 20 Gb/s Thunderbolt Networking over a Thunderbolt 4 or 3 cable.
standout_why: WunderTech (cited) covers the Synology card pairings (E10G22-T1-Mini for DS1525+, E10G30-T1 for DS1825+, none for DS925+), Synology's SSD-list rule for M.2 pools, and UGREEN's Thunderbolt firmware floor (UGOS 1.2.0.2121), so those are already taken. Esp32.co.uk (cited) says QNAP Thunderbolt networking reaches 20 Gb/s and that the Lockerstor 6 Gen3 has 'USB4, not Thunderbolt', but never says the USB4 port cannot host-link a computer, and gives no macOS floor or cable rule. Neither rival nor the other ten results states the Asustor exclusion or the QNAP macOS 13.5 requirement, and none has the UGREEN store's own prices for today.
decides: It confirms the UGREEN DXP6800 Pro as the pick for a solo editor who wants one cable to the workstation: the maker-supported direct-link field is UGREEN (DXP6800 Pro, DXP8800 Plus, DXP480T Plus) and QNAP's T-series (TVS-h874T/h674T, TBS-h574TX). Asustor's Flashstor and Lockerstor Gen2/Gen3, TerraMaster and Synology are 10GbE-only for a host link, so their 'USB4' spec line should not sway a Mac editor. For QNAP buyers, a Mac must be on macOS 13.5 or later and the link is capped at 20 Gb/s regardless of the 40 Gb/s port rating; on the TVS-h874T the Thunderbolt card also consumes one of the two PCIe slots, leaving one for a 10/25GbE card.

findings.label: USB4 host link to a PC or Mac
findings.value: Not supported; USB4 is limited to external storage devices and a direct link to another Lockerstor Gen3 or Flashstor Gen2
findings.source_title: ASUSTOR knowledge base: Can I connect my PC or Mac to my ASUSTOR NAS using USB4?
findings.note: Maker FAQ text: 'The Lockerstor Gen3 and Flashstor Gen2 series are based on AMD's current USB4 driver. AMD USB4 at the moment only supports external storage devices and direct connection between another Lockerstor Gen3 or Flashstor Gen2 series NAS.' Replaces the 'Mac bridge unverified' wording in our Asustor rows; host access is via the 10GbE/5GbE ports only.

findings.label: Thunderbolt Networking bandwidth cap
findings.value: 20 Gb/s maximum per link (ports are Thunderbolt 4)
findings.note: Page text: 'adopts Thunderbolt Networking technology and provides maximum bandwidth of 20 Gbps.' Two Thunderbolt 4 Type-C ports standard.

findings.label: Supported host computers and minimum macOS
findings.value: Apple silicon Macs (M1, M2 named), Intel Macs and Windows PCs; macOS 13.5 or later
findings.note: Page text: 'works perfectly with Macs using Apple Silicon (such as M1 and M2 chips) and Intel processors, and Windows PCs' and 'System requirement: macOS 13.5 (or later)'. No Windows driver or cable requirement stated on the page.

findings.label: PCIe slot consumed by Thunderbolt
findings.value: 1 of 2 PCIe Gen 4 slots is occupied by the dual Thunderbolt 4 card; the other takes up to a 25GbE card
findings.note: Stated in a Profesional Review excerpt that QNAP reproduces on its own product page, not in QNAP's spec table. QNAP's page lists compatible cards: QXG-10G2T, QXG-10G1T, QXG-10G2T-X710, QXG-10G2SF-NXE, QXG-10G2SF-X710 (10GbE), QXG-25G2SF-CX6 and QXG-25G2SF-E810 (25GbE), QM2-2P10G1TB (M.2 + 10GbE).

findings.label: Thunderbolt host link: bandwidth, hosts, macOS floor, cable
findings.value: Up to 20 Gb/s Thunderbolt Networking; Mac (M1 and M2 named) or Windows workstations; macOS 13.5 or later; Thunderbolt 4 or Thunderbolt 3 cable
findings.note: Page text: 'QNAP Thunderbolt NAS adopts Thunderbolt Networking for peer-to-peer connection, up to 20Gbps'; 'Mac system requirement: macOS 13.5 (or later)'; 'Connect the TBS-h574TX to your Mac or Windows PC with Thunderbolt 4 / Thunderbolt 3 cables'. Two Thunderbolt 4 ports.

findings.label: SSD form-factor pairing
findings.value: 5× E1.S PCIe NVMe bays; M.2 2280 SSDs fit only via the optional QDA-E1SM E1.S tray with M.2 adapter
findings.note: Page text: '5 x E1.S PCIe NVMe slots (M.2 2280 supported)' and 'Optional E1.S to M.2 SSD adapter enables hot-swappable M.2 SSD installation'; accessory listed as 'E1.S Tray w/ M.2 2280 adapter for TBS series NAS' (QDA-E1SM). Hot-swap is stated for E1.S drives.
